newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo Sartid to privatise in autumn - official.
newsitem.headline: Yugo Sartid to privatise in autumn - official.

text.p: Yugoslavia's iron and steel mill Sartid of Smederevo will begin a lengthy and complex ownership transformation process in autumn this year, a ruling Serbian Socialist Party (SPS) official said on Friday.
"The privatisation process in Sartid will start next October," Dusan Matkovic, president of the SPS Council for Economic Reforms, told a news conference.
Matkovic said the company's privatisation programme was made more than year and a half ago with a help of Deloitte & Touche consulting firm.
"We have assessed the value of the capital too. But, I assume it would be some $1.5 billion now," said Matkovic, till recently Sartid's chief executive.
Serbia on Thursday presented a final version of its first draft privatisation law expected to be passed by the end of the month. It is to become effective from October 31.
Under the law, strategically important state-controlled companies like Sartid will be transformed under a special programme and need government approval.
Matkovic said there were few foreign partners interested to obtain company's shares through capitalisation.
"There is one partner from Germany and one from Italy who are ready to invest $100 million each," Matkovic said but declined to give any more details.
He said the privatisation of Sartid steel works would last for a long time. "Privatisation of steel works is a very complex issue".
After a virtual standstill of nearly four years due to the international war-related sanctions imposed on Yugoslavia in May 1992, production in Smederevo complex restarted in March last year.
The company produced 750,000 tonnes of steel and steel plates and sheets by the end of March this year thanks to foreign credits approved by banks from Switzerland and Lebanon.
The bulk of Sartid's 1996 production worth $85 million was exported.
The plant's export income in January stood at $20 million and in February $15 million.
The company plans to produce one million tonnes of steel and steel products in 1997. -- Gordana Kukic, Belgrade Newsroom +381 11 222 4254
